entry.title: [bijanabdolkarimi] When I used to go on patrol during the war, I was proud, and I wished it would…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @bijanabdolkarimi

When I used to go on patrol during the war, I was proud, and I wished it would never end — until we took revenge for the blood of the martyrs from Israel. But on 19 Dey, there was only shame — I wanted it to end. I wanted to take off the vest and stand before the crowd and say, stop... The thieves are eating your bread — those on this side, along with their dream of life — and they are eating bread and scheming — those on that side — and you are drowning in the dream of revenge... Is it only for revenge that you want justice? What can I say... Perhaps this is the hardest period of my life, perhaps I will not emerge from this challenge with my head held high. I wish it were the 1360s and I were seeking the dream of the embrace of martyrdom with the headband of Ya Zahra among the trenches. I wish at least on 19 Dey that Pars car that was coming toward me had run me over and this nightmare would have ended... But still, a glimmer of the candle of hope is lit. One day I will reach my beloved. My country's flag dances with joy in the sky. My people are proud of being Iranian. The sound of the adhan comes from the mosque and all become devoted, and from the God of their own selves, the Creator of their sufferings, they are freed and dissolve into the absolute good of existence... Perhaps here, perhaps elsewhere... A note for the professor...
---
